question_text: Find the equation of locus of P, if the line segment joining (4,0) and (0,4) subtends a right angle at P.

recall_prompt: Say how you would solve this — name the condition you would write for the right angle, and say what shape the locus turns out to be.

steps.label: Take the locus point
steps.margin_note: No mark of its own, but nothing below can be written without it. P is the point that moves; A and B are nailed down.
steps.memory_tip: P moves; A and B are fixed.
lines: Let P = (x, y) be a point on the locus.

recall.must_convey: That the moving point is named P = (x, y) and the fixed points are written down.
accept: let P be x comma y
take the locus point as P x y
P equals x comma y is on the locus
locus point ni P x y ga teesukovali
name the moving point P with coordinates x and y

steps.why: Every locus question starts the same way: the moving point gets coordinates, and the condition is then written in terms of those coordinates.
common_mistakes: Giving the moving point fixed numbers instead of (x, y).
Mixing up which points are fixed and which one moves.

steps.label: Write the given condition
steps.margin_note: First mark. A right angle at P means the triangle APB is right angled AT P, so AB is its hypotenuse and Pythagoras applies as PA² + PB² = AB². Writing this line earns the mark on its own.
steps.memory_tip: Right angle at P makes AB the hypotenuse, so PA² + PB² = AB².

recall.must_convey: That the right angle at P is turned into PA² + PB² = AB².
accept: angle A P B is ninety so P A squared plus P B squared equals A B squared
use pythagoras with A B as the hypotenuse
right angle at P means P A square plus P B square is A B square
ninety degrees kabatti P A square plus P B square equals A B square
apply pythagoras theorem to the triangle
heard_as: P A squared plus P B squared

steps.why: A right angle at a point is almost never used as an angle in this chapter — it is used as Pythagoras. PA² + PB² = AB² turns the angle into distances, and distances are what coordinates can express.
common_mistakes: Writing PA² + AB² = PB², which puts the right angle at the wrong vertex.
Trying to use the slope condition m₁m₂ = −1 and then losing the sign.

steps.label: Substitute the distances
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Every distance becomes the square of a coordinate difference, and because the condition is already squared there is no square root anywhere in this line.
steps.memory_tip: Already squared, so no roots in this line.

recall.must_convey: That each distance is replaced by its coordinate form using the distance formula, squared.
accept: substitute the distance formula for each of P A, P B and A B
put x minus x one whole squared plus y minus y one whole squared for each distance
write every distance in coordinates without the root
distance formula apply chesi coordinates lo rasukovali
replace the distances with the coordinate expressions

steps.why: PA² is written straight from the distance formula as (x−x₁)² + (y−y₁)², with no root sign, because the condition was stated in squares.
common_mistakes: Leaving a square root in, then having to square the whole line again.
Subtracting the coordinates the wrong way round inside a bracket that is not squared yet.

steps.label: Simplify to the locus
steps.margin_note: The last two marks. Expand, cancel, and every x² and y² term survives with the SAME coefficient — that is what identifies the locus as a circle. Divide by that coefficient to finish.
steps.memory_tip: Equal x² and y² coefficients means a circle — divide by that coefficient to finish.

lines.text: ∴ Locus of P is x² + y² − 4x − 4y = 0

recall.must_convey: That expanding and cancelling gives the circle x² + y² − 4x − 4y = 0.
accept: expand everything and cancel to get the circle
simplify and divide by two to get the equation of the locus
after cancelling the constants the x squared and y squared coefficients match so it is a circle
expand chesi simplify chesthe circle equation vasthundi
the locus is a circle

steps.why: The locus of a point that sees a fixed segment at a right angle is the circle on that segment as diameter, so a circle is the expected shape and a check on the algebra.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to divide by the common factor 2 at the end.
Losing a sign when expanding a bracket like (y − 4)².
